purpose: Neutral, general-English homophone / soundalike name spelling-variant groups for (a) a transcription/parse LLM that HEARS names, and (b) a customer-lookup matcher. When a name is heard, these give every plausible spelling so the system can surface all candidates AND pick the one that matches an existing client, email, or spelled-out letters. This is the CURATED override layer that complements an automatic phonetic key (Metaphone/Double Metaphone) and the nickname map (nickname_root). It ships with NO tenant records; a business's own confirmed spellings and de-dup pairs layer in through the zdz_name_homophones_map filter (an Identity Pack), never here.

how_to_use.for_the_transcription_llm: When you hear a name, do NOT lock a single spelling from the sound alone. Emit the heard sound plus the candidate spellings from the matching group, then choose using the contextual_pick priority below. If two spellings both plausibly exist, keep the one the context supports and flag needs_review.
how_to_use.for_the_matcher: Expand a queried name to its whole group before matching so any spelling in the group co-surfaces as a suggestion. Two names in the same group are CONFUSABLE (show both), not necessarily the SAME person (never auto-merge without an email/phone/address match). Auto-fill still requires a self-entered identifier match (INV-12).
contextual_pick_priority: 1. SPELLED-OUT LETTERS WIN. If the speaker spells it, that beats the sound, always.
2. EMAIL LOCAL-PART. Match the spelling to the customer's own email (a 'jon@' local part supports 'Jon' over 'John'). The email is the field the customer typed themselves.
3. EXISTING CLIENT. If a client with one of the spellings already exists in the connected system of record - especially with a matching email/phone/address - use that spelling.
5. LAST RESORT. Use the most common spelling AND set needs_review; NEVER silently merge two distinct clients that only sound alike.
how_to_use.engineering_note: Best practice is two layers: an automatic phonetic key (PHP metaphone()/soundex(), or Double Metaphone) catches the long tail (many soundalikes such as Reed=Read or Smith=Smyth map to the same key for free); this curated list handles what the algorithm gets wrong - near-homophones the key splits, cross-lingual ones, short-vowel pairs the length-gated Levenshtein misses (e.g. a five-letter name vs its four-letter variant), and pairs that MUST stay distinct.

surnames.note: short-vowel confusable (Ben-der vs Bin-der); keep distinct unless email/phone confirms

given_names.note: spans first-name and can collide with a surname

data_provenance_caveat: This is a neutral, general-English seed. It contains NO tenant customer records: no spelling here is asserted to be a real customer of any business. A tenant's own confirmed spellings (which spelling a real client uses), same-sound-different-business pairs (distinct_but_confusable), and de-dup targets are private data and load at runtime via the zdz_name_homophones_map filter from an Identity Pack — they are never shipped in this file.
